press.text: Listen, I'm going to be straight with you — that's how I operate. Border Bore-Casc is right between us, and if we both race for it, we both lose time while everyone else grows. Here's my deal: you focus on Border Aval-Bore, I take Border Bore-Casc, and we establish a real non-aggression line. We can both grow into Year 2 strong instead of banging our heads together on Day One. I'm not interested in fighting my neighbor when there's a whole map to carve up. What do you say?

I'm coming to you straight, no games: Border Casc-Delt sits right between our two nations. If we both charge at it this spring, we bounce, look weak, and let everyone else get ahead. I'm proposing we each focus outward — you go hard for Border Delt-East, I take Border Casc-Delt, and we hold a clean line between us. No aggression, no tricks. I want a strong Deltara on my flank more than I want a fight. Work with me here.

Eastmark — I'm Cascadia's President, and I'm looking at this board strategically. You and I don't share a border, which means we have zero reason to be enemies and every reason to talk. While our respective neighbors are all jostling for border scraps, I think there's an opportunity for powers like ours — who aren't right on top of each other — to coordinate on the bigger picture. Open to a real conversation if you are.

Greetings from Grenmar. I want to open this game the right way — with direct, honest communication between neighbors. We share the Border Fjor-Gren province, and I think it's in both our interests to avoid a costly collision there in Year 1 when there are easier gains elsewhere. I'm proposing a simple arrangement: you take Border Fjor-Gren, I take Border Gren-Aval, and we both secure our respective Cores. No conflict, mutual growth. Beyond that, I see real value in a lasting alliance — Grenmar and Fjordland working together rather than bleeding each other dry. Tell me what you're thinking. I'm listening.

President Newsom here, reaching out from Grenmar. First order of business: I don't believe in ambiguous signals between neighbors. We share Border Gren-Aval, and rather than race toward it and potentially bounce, I'd like us to coordinate. My proposal: I move toward Border Gren-Aval with your blessing and support — or we split the region cleanly in a way that works for both of us. More broadly, I think a Grenmar-Avalon partnership has real strategic legs. We're adjacent, we're both capable powers, and a stable western side of the wheel frees us to engage more decisively elsewhere. What are your priorities this opening year?

Gavin Newsom, Grenmar. Reaching out early because I believe in building relationships before they're needed. You're across the wheel from me — no immediate territorial tension — which makes you a natural candidate for a strategic partnership. I'm playing a coalition-oriented game, not a solo land-grab. If you're interested in coordinating on broader board strategy as Year 1 unfolds, I'd value that. What's your read on the opening?

Grenmar reaching out. Early days, but I want to make sure every leadership is in communication from the start. No immediate shared border between us, which means we can build a relationship based on strategic interest rather than necessity. I'm keeping an eye on the full picture here — interested in your perspective on how the board is shaping up. Open to coordination as opportunities emerge.

President Newsom of Grenmar. Reaching out to all powers in the opening round — transparency and early communication are how I operate. We're not immediate neighbors, which gives us room to build something durable without the friction that comes with shared borders. I'd welcome an ongoing dialogue as the year unfolds. What are your strategic priorities?

Grenmar here. Beginning the game the way I intend to continue it — with open lines of communication to every power on the board. You're adjacent to Fjordland, who is my neighbor, so we share an indirect interest in how that part of the wheel develops. I'm committed to a cooperative approach where possible and looking for partners who think the same way. Happy to talk strategy whenever you're ready.

Greetings from Borealis. As neighbors, we face a clear choice in Year 1: race each other to Border Aval-Bore and waste energy, or partition sensibly. I propose a clean arrangement: Borealis takes no aggressive action toward Avalon, and you do the same. We each take our 'near' neutral centers and grow in our natural directions — you toward Grenmar, me toward Cascadia. I have no designs on your territory. A stable western flank benefits us both. Interested in a non-aggression pact for at least Year 1?

Hello from Borealis. I'll be direct: Year 1 is about securing your position, not making enemies. I'm proposing to both my neighbors that we avoid mutual bleeding. For us specifically: I'm willing to let the Border Bore-Casc situation settle without a fight if we can agree to a non-aggression understanding. Your natural expansion runs toward Deltara; mine runs toward Avalon. There's no reason for Borealis and Cascadia to be the ones grinding each other down in Year 1 while everyone else builds up. What are your intentions?

Distant greeting from Borealis. We don't share a border, which makes this an ideal time to talk honestly. I'm watching how the wheel develops. Eastmark and Grenmar are your immediate neighbors — how is that looking from your side? I'm interested in sharing intelligence and potentially coordinating strategy with powers that aren't in direct competition with me. No commitments yet — just opening a channel.

Hey — this is Alexandria from Eastmark. I want to start this the right way: with honesty and direct communication. We're neighbors, and how we handle our shared border matters a lot.

My proposal: we each move toward Border Delt-East from our own side — you take it if you get there first, I'll take it if I do — and we agree right now on a hard line: no Eastmark units cross west of that border, no Deltara units cross east of it. We formalize a non-aggression pact and focus our energy outward.

I'm genuinely not interested in a grinding battle with you. I'd rather we both grow and deal with the powers on our far flanks. What are your thoughts? Who are you worried about on your other side?

Hi — Alexandria, Eastmark here. First Year, so let's set the tone right.

You're my eastern neighbor. I want to propose a clean, mutual arrangement: we each secure our side of Border East-Fjor without contesting it, and we commit to a non-aggression line along that border. I have no ambitions eastward into your territory — I need to focus on my own development and the Core.

I'd rather have a trusted partner on my eastern flank than spend resources fighting a war of attrition with you. Open to a formal pact. What's your read on the overall board — who do you think is going to make an early aggressive push?

Hello from Eastmark — Alexandria here. You're two steps away from me on the wheel, so we're not directly competing for territory in the early game. That makes you exactly the kind of power I want a relationship with.

I'm a firm believer that early diplomatic contacts shape the whole arc of a game. I wanted to reach out, introduce myself, and ask: what's your read on the board? Any powers you're concerned about? I'm especially watching for anyone who makes an early all-out aggressive move — those powers need to be checked collectively.

Hope we can stay in regular contact.

Hi — Alexandria from Eastmark. We're neighbors-once-removed on the wheel, which means we have a real opportunity to build something without the immediate border tensions that come with direct adjacency.

I'm reaching out early because I believe in proactive diplomacy over reactive crisis management. I'd love to hear your read on things — who do you think poses the biggest threat to balance on the board? I'm committed to not being an aggressor, and I'd love to know if we can count on a similar philosophy from you.

Let's stay in touch.

Hello — this is Alexandria, President of Eastmark. We're on opposite sides of the wheel, which actually makes us natural long-distance partners. No territorial conflicts, no border disputes — just mutual interest in keeping the game balanced.

I'm reaching out to everyone early because I think the biggest danger in Year 1 is that powers at opposite ends of the wheel get dragged into wars by their neighbors' maneuvering. I'd like us to stay in communication and share information about aggressive moves we're seeing. 

What's your read on the early game?

Hi — Alexandria from Eastmark. We're fairly distant on the wheel, so I'm reaching out simply to establish a communication channel and share perspectives.

I'm playing a cooperative, coalition-focused game — I'd rather build a broad, stable network of relationships than pursue rapid unilateral expansion. I'd love to hear your read on who seems most aggressive early on, and whether there's any arrangement that might benefit both of us down the line.

Hope to hear from you.

Hello from Deltara. I want to open a direct channel early — that's just how I prefer to operate. We share a border center, and I think it's in both our interests to avoid a contested opening that bleeds us both. My proposal: you take Border Casc-Delt this spring without interference from me; I orient my expansion eastward toward Border Delt-East. We both grow efficiently, and we build some baseline trust. I'm genuinely interested in a longer-term working relationship if the early moves bear it out. What are you thinking?

Reaching out early — I think transparent communication makes for better outcomes than surprises. We're neighbors, and Border Delt-East is a natural point of friction. I'd like to propose we each take 'our' border center uncontested — I move toward Border Delt-East, you move toward Border East-Fjor — and we keep the middle de-escalated. I'm not looking to squeeze you from the west while you manage the east. Looking forward to hearing your read on the situation.

Greetings from Deltara. We're at opposite ends of the wheel, which I think makes us natural partners rather than rivals — at least in the near term. I'm interested in building a communication channel and potentially coordinating on the bigger strategic picture as the game develops. No pressure this early, but I'd like to know your thinking. What's your read on the opening?

Hello — Deltara here. We're near-antipodal on the wheel, which means we're not competing for the same territory and have real potential for a durable working relationship. I'm keeping my options open but want to establish trust with the powers I'm not directly bumping into. Interested in keeping a line open and comparing notes as things unfold?

Deltara reaching out. We're two steps apart, which puts us in an interesting position — not immediate rivals, but close enough that coordination matters. I'm curious what your opening posture looks like and whether there's a framework that benefits us both. Happy to share more about my intentions if you're open to a dialogue.

Deltara here — wanted to open a line of communication early. You're two steps east of me, so our immediate interests don't collide, but I think mid-game dynamics will matter a lot and I'd rather have relationships built before they're needed. What's your read on the opening situation? Interested in comparing notes.

This is President Rubio. Strong nations talk straight, so here it is: I have no hostile intentions toward Borealis, and I think we both know the smart play in Year 1 is to avoid bleeding each other while other powers consolidate unchecked. I'm planning to expand westward toward Grenmar's flank — that's my natural direction. I'd propose we each respect a clean line: you secure Border Bore-Casc and build east, I secure my western approaches. Border Aval-Bore sits in a contested zone — let's discuss a framework so neither of us wastes strength there. A Borealis-Avalon non-aggression pact frees us both to be forces to reckon with. Interested?

President Rubio here. I believe in clarity, so let me offer some: Avalon and Grenmar don't have to be adversaries. The wheel rewards those who pick the right partners early. I'm reaching out because I'd rather build a productive relationship with you than have us stumble into conflict while Fjordland or others make moves neither of us anticipates. Tell me what your priorities are this year — I'm genuinely interested in finding common ground and potentially coordinating. Strength through alliance beats grinding each other down.

President Rubio reaching out. Fjordland and Avalon are on opposite ends of the wheel — we don't compete for the same territory, and that's exactly the basis for a real, durable alliance. I've seen how these games go: powers on opposite arcs who trust each other and coordinate can dominate the board while the middle tires itself out. I want to establish that kind of relationship with you early. What's your read on the emerging threats? I suspect powers consolidating in the middle of the wheel should concern us both.

Rubio here. Early communication wins games — I'm reaching out to every power I consider a potential partner, and Eastmark is on that list. We're far enough apart to have no immediate conflict, close enough in interest to coordinate. Who worries you most right now? I have some thoughts on the emerging balance of power and I'd value your perspective before moves are locked in.

President Rubio, Avalon bloc. I believe in building bridges with capable partners early. Deltara is positioned in an interesting part of the wheel — your moves this year will shape the whole board. I'd like to open a dialogue. I'm not approaching you with demands, just with a genuine interest in understanding your goals and seeing if our interests align. Strong alliances are forged at the start, not salvaged at the end.

Rubio here — just establishing contact. Avalon is not looking for conflict with Cascadia. We're far enough apart that we should be natural friends, not rivals. I'd like to keep communication open and discuss how we can each grow without getting in each other's way. Looking forward to hearing from you.

President Vance here. Look, let's cut to it — we're neighbors, and neither of us benefits from a fight while there are free centers sitting unclaimed. Here's my offer: you take Border Delt-East, I take Border East-Fjor. We stay out of each other's lanes, expand in our own directions. No complicated alliances, no strings. Just two powers acting in their own clear interests. I'm not looking for a war on my doorstep in Year 1 — but I'm also not going to blink if someone pushes. Your call.

Vance, Fjordland. Simple proposition: you take Border Gren-Aval, I take Border Fjor-Gren. We each look outward, not at each other. I've got no interest in grinding through your territory when there's easier ground elsewhere — and I'd assume you feel the same. Let's agree to a clean western frontier and build from there. I keep my word when the deal makes sense. This one does.

JD Vance, Fjordland. We're not neighbors so we've got no immediate friction — which makes this a good time to talk. The powers that move first and coordinate smart are the ones that end up with 18 centers. I'm not looking for a formal alliance yet, but I want a line of communication open with Borealis. What's your read on the board? Who are you watching?

- Border Casc-Delt (between Cascadia and Deltara)

Playing as a nationalist power, I'll be direct and aggressive about territorial expansion, willing to make deals when tactically useful but not bound by them if circumstances change. I need to think through the mechanics of border control more carefully. So my strategy should be to negotiate with my neighbors—getting Borealis to stay away from Border Bore-Casc while I move there, and doing the same with Deltara on my other flank. This way I can secure both borders without direct conflict, at least in the opening moves.

I'm also considering which units can push toward Core Cascadia, the central territory that's probably accessible through East and West Cascadia. I'm drafting an opening message to Borealis suggesting we divide the contested borders and potentially ally against common threats. I should reach out to each neighbor with tailored proposals: offer Borealis the Border Aval-Bore center while I take Border Bore-Casc, suggest to Deltara that I get Border Casc-Delt and they secure Border Delt-East, and feel out potential allies further afield. I'll approach this with confidence and directness, making it clear these are mutually beneficial arrangements.

**Private Reasoning:**

Alright, let me assess this board. It's a wheel — I'm Cascadia, flanked by Borealis to one side and Deltara to the other. My immediate uncontested goals: grab Core Cascadia, Border Bore-Casc, and Border Casc-Delt. That gets me to 6 centers if I clean sweep.

The problem: if Borealis races for Border Bore-Casc and Deltara races for Border Casc-Delt simultaneously, we all bounce and I'm stuck at 3. I need to do some fast-talking to get one or both neighbors to back off those contested spaces.

As MTG — I'm going in direct and confident. I'm not playing some globalist coalition game. I'm making deals that benefit Cascadia. I'll pitch coordination to both neighbors (you take YOUR other border, let me take mine), and reach out to Eastmark as a potential far-ally since they're across the wheel and we don't compete directly.

Actually, the smarter play is to position Fort and Port for Fall captures rather than wasting a support order on a neutral province—I'll move Fort to East Cascadia and Port to West Cascadia to set up for the next season, while City holds back since I can't split it between two moves.

Let me just settle on concrete Spring orders: City moves to East Cascadia to position toward either Core Cascadia or the Deltara border, while Fort and Port handle their own movements. Fort can move into East Cascadia once City vacates it, giving me better positioning for Year 2. So my final orders are: City pushes to East Cascadia, Port secures the Borealis border route, and Fort holds to maintain home control—then Fort advances in Fall once City moves deeper into enemy territory. I'll go with Fort and Port as my flanking units pushing outward while City holds the center—this keeps my home secure and positions me to capture border territories in the Fall. Grenmar.press:
Let me analyze the board situation at the start of Year 1, Spring.

**Map Structure:**
The map is a wheel of 7 powers. Each power has 3 home centers. There are 35 supply centers total:
- 21 home centers (3 per power)
- 7 Border centers (one between each adjacent pair)
- 7 Core centers (one per power's "core" region)

**My position - Grenmar:**
- Units: Grenmar City, Grenmar Fort, Grenmar Port
- Adjacent to: Border Fjor-Gren (between Fjordland and Grenmar) and Border Gren-Aval (between Grenmar and Avalon)
- Core Grenmar is also unowned

From my three units, I can reach East Grenmar, West Grenmar, and the two border centers adjacent to my territory. I need to determine which of these border centers I can actually move into and what my best opening moves are.

Looking at the wheel structure, Grenmar sits between Fjordland and Avalon, so Border Fjor-Gren connects me westward and Border Gren-Aval connects me eastward. Now I'm thinking through my diplomatic approach as Newsom—I should prioritize building strong alliances early, being transparent about my intentions, and leveraging science-based decision-making to establish credibility with other powers.

My immediate strategy is to reach out to both neighbors with non-aggression pacts and cooperation agreements, while also sounding out more distant powers for broader coalitions. The critical decision is whether to push first into the western border territory toward Fjordland or the eastern one toward Avalon, depending on which neighbor seems more receptive to a cooperative expansion rather than conflict. "I should reach out to Fjordland about establishing a non-aggression pact and coordinating on our shared border centers, then do the same with Avalon. As Gavin, I'd be proactive and warm in my diplomacy—building trust and gathering information while keeping my military strategy close to the vest."

## Strategic Assessment — Spring, Year 1

**The Board:** A 7-power wheel. I'm Grenmar, sitting between Fjordland (left) and Avalon (right). The unowned centers I can realistically reach first are: **Core Grenmar**, **Border Fjor-Gren**, and **Border Gren-Aval**. Every power is in the same symmetric starting position — this is a pure coordination and trust game early on.

**My Priorities:**
1. Secure Core Grenmar — unambiguously mine to take
2. Coordinate with Fjordland and Avalon on the shared border provinces — conflict there helps neither of us
3. Build early diplomatic relationships across the wheel; broader coalitions beat bilateral deals
4. Avoid being the power everyone else gangs up on

**Diplomatic Logic:**
- Reach out to *everyone* — Gavin Newsom doesn't leave calls unreturned
- With neighbors (Fjordland, Avalon): propose non-aggression and coordination, float the idea of a formal alliance
- With middle-wheel powers (Borealis, Cascadia, Deltara, Eastmark): establish rapport, signal I'm a reliable partner, probe their intentions
- Don't overcommit yet — information is scarce in Round 1

**Map Analysis:**
I'm checking my current holdings and what's adjacent to them. I control Grenmar City, Grenmar Fort, and Grenmar Port, and I need to trace out which unowned centers I can reach, particularly Core Grenmar, though the adjacency data seems incomplete in my notes.

Core Grenmar isn't showing up in any direct adjacency lists, which suggests it might be two moves away rather than immediately reachable. Looking at the wheel structure with seven powers, each having three home centers plus border and core territories, I need to figure out whether East and West Grenmar are actually the border provinces or if they're intermediate non-supply-center territories that connect to the real borders. Grenmar are adjacent to Core Grenmar, so I need to position units there in Spring to be ready for a Fall capture. The real strategy is that I'm aiming for three supply centers by Fall—Core Grenmar, Border Gren-Aval, and Border Fjor-Gren—which would give me six total. Fjordland and I have already agreed he'll take Border Fjor-Gren while I secure Border Gren-Aval, so I need to plan my Spring moves accordingly to make that happen. Since Grenmar City can reach either East or West Grenmar, and the Fort and Port have more limited options, I need to figure out which direction each unit should move to efficiently control both Border Gren-Aval and Border Fjor-Gren while also pushing toward Core Grenmar. So Grenmar City should probably just hold in place since there's no immediate threat to defend against, but if it moves to either East or West Grenmar it'll collide with Fort or Port respectively. The real question is whether City should support one of those advances or stay put—though supporting might not matter much in Spring Year 1 since the board isn't under pressure yet.

Given my agreements with Fjordland and Avalon, I shouldn't face conflicts at the borders, so the safest play is to push Fort toward the Gren-Aval side and Port toward the Fjor-Gren side, positioning myself to control Core Grenmar from multiple directions by Fall. If City moves to where Fort was, that's pointless since Fort is already leaving. The same goes for moving to Port's old position. But if both City and Fort try to move to East Grenmar, they'd bounce and stay put. So the cleanest approach is to have Fort advance east, Port advance west, and City hold its ground—unless there's a strategic reason to support Fort's move if Avalon poses a threat, though they've indicated they want to cooperate.

For Spring Year 1, there's really no immediate danger to home centers, so I can afford to be aggressive. Looking at the adjacency map, East Grenmar and West Grenmar are the border areas with no hostile threats immediately accessible from City itself. I'll stick with Fort moving east, Port moving west, and City holding position.

Now I need to submit these orders through the system.

## Strategic Reasoning — Spring Year 1 Orders

**Reading the inbox:**
- **Fjordland (Vance)**: Proposing exactly the deal I offered — he takes Border Fjor-Gren, I take Border Gren-Aval. Clean symmetry. I trust the logic if not necessarily the person.
- **Avalon (Rubio)**: Wants partnership, signals openness to coordination. Promising, though Rubio warrants watching.
- **Eastmark (AOC)**: Friendly, ideologically adjacent, asks about threats. Natural long-range partner.
- **Deltara (Buttigieg)**: Professional outreach, wants open lines. Good.

**Board geometry:**
- Grenmar Fort can only practically reach East Grenmar from its position
- Grenmar Port can only practically reach West Grenmar
- Grenmar City sits at the hub — best used to hold the center or as future support

**Move logic:**
- Push Fort east (toward Border Gren-Aval direction) — sets up Fall capture
- Push Port west (toward Border Fjor-Gren direction) — consistent with Fjordland deal
- Hold City at home — no threats to home center in Year 1, keeps it as anchor and support option

I'm NOT trying to grab both border centers AND the Core in Year 1 — that would require splitting too thin. This Spring positioning sets up a clean 3-center Fall: Core Grenmar + both borders if the deals hold, or at minimum Core + one border.

They lied to my face about non-aggression last turn and grabbed everything they could. Now they're positioned right against your territory. I'm not sitting next to a liar who grows fat off broken promises. I think it's time we talk seriously about coordinating against Borealis before they become a real problem for both of us. I've got units on their eastern flank. You've got pressure from the west. Let's not let Borealis snowball.

You broke your word. We can talk about what that means going forward, or we can just acknowledge that it happened and reset. I'm not here to cry about it — I expected nothing less from someone who operates the way you do. But understand this: Border Bore-Casc is not yours. If you come for it, you'll pay for it. I'd rather we both walk away from that contested space and expand in other directions. You want Avalon? Go take Avalon. I'll stay east of Bore-Casc. But if you push west into my territory, I'll make sure it costs you more than it's worth.

Pete — you kept your word and I respect that. Let's formalize what we have: a stable western line for you, a stable eastern line for me. I'm not interested in pushing into your territory. I want Core Cascadia and I want to build from there. I'd like to propose a genuine non-aggression pact through Year 3 — both of us hold the Casc-Delt border stable, expand outward in other directions, and we can revisit the relationship from a position of strength. Are you in?

Gavin — let me give you my honest read: Fjordland at 4 centers already, and they grabbed Border Fjor-Gren which is basically your front door. That's a threat you should be taking seriously. You're at 3, they're at 4 and positioned against you. I've got no beef with Grenmar. If you need a friend who can help stabilize your position while you deal with Fjordland's pressure, I'm open to a serious conversation. What are you thinking?

Alexandria — you mentioned you're watching Fjordland, and so am I. They grabbed Border Fjor-Gren in Year 1, which puts them up against Grenmar. Four centers already. I notice you're working with Deltara — that's your call. But I'd rather have you as a genuine partner than a distant acquaintance. If Fjordland keeps growing on the south end of the wheel, that's everyone's problem eventually. What's your read on them?

JD — let me be direct about Year 1. You contested East-Fjor after proposing I stand down from it. We bounced, neither of us grew from it, and you ended up taking Fjor-Gren instead. No hard feelings — you made your play — but I need you to understand I'm not going to be moved off East-Fjor. I'm going there again this year.

Here's the deal I'm actually offering: take Core Fjordland. That's YOUR core center, it's on your natural expansion path, and I'm not contesting it. You grow to five, I get East-Fjor and grow to four. Clean split, real growth for both of us.

If you move West Fjordland at East-Fjor again, we bounce again, and we both lose a year while Borealis and Cascadia are at four and building momentum. That's a bad outcome for both of us. Think about it.

Pete — I want to say this plainly: I supported your move to Border Delt-East when I didn't have to. I could have taken it myself, or contested, or just held. I chose to back you up because I meant what I said about building a real alliance.

Now I need that to mean something. I'm at 3 centers while almost everyone else is at 4. I need East-Fjor this year. I'm asking you to do two things:

1) Keep your western units from pointing at my territory — I already know you're not aggressive toward me, but I want it confirmed.
2) If there's any way your units can support my move to East-Fjor — even indirectly by keeping Fjordland occupied on their western flank — I'd call that a real act of partnership.

In return: I will support your push toward Core Deltara when the time comes. You have my commitment on that.

Gavin — yes, I want to formalize this Grenmar-Eastmark alignment. Here's why it's urgent: JD Vance just built a new unit AT Border Fjor-Gren. He's in your territory. He grew to four while we're both sitting at three.

He's going to try to use that unit to either take Core Grenmar or squeeze you. You need to contest him now, before he consolidates. And I need to take Border East-Fjor before he locks it down from the west.

Here's what I propose: you push your western unit toward Border Fjor-Gren to contest JD's presence there, and I push east to Border East-Fjor. JD is caught between us — he can't reinforce both directions. We both grow, he doesn't.

Are you in? This is the move.

Marjorie — my honest read on the biggest threat: Borealis. They got Border Aval-Bore and built to four. They're positioned between Avalon and your territory. If they push into Border Bore-Casc, they're directly pressuring you. Worth thinking about.

I'm focused on securing my eastern border right now. What's your read on Borealis's intentions? And what are you planning on your eastern flank near Deltara?

Marco — updating you on my read. Four powers are at four centers: Borealis, Cascadia, Deltara, Fjordland. Grenmar and I are still at three. That's the imbalance developing. 

Borealis grew into Border Aval-Bore — that's your doorstep. Are you concerned? I'd be. The power that grabs two border centers and starts rolling into cores early is the one we should all be watching. 

What's your plan for Year 2? I want to stay in sync.

Alexandria — you kept your word in Year 1, and that matters. I'm going to be equally straight with you now: my priority this year is Core Deltara. It's adjacent to my position at Border Delt-East, and it's the natural next move for me. I'm not threatening you — I'm moving inward, not toward Eastmark. What I'd ask in return is that you point toward Core Eastmark or Border East-Fjor, which are still open, rather than toward the same space. We can both grow without stepping on each other. What's your read on the eastern end of the board right now? Fjordland is at 4 and has Border Fjor-Gren — that seems like your bigger concern.

Marjorie — Year 1 went exactly as we discussed, and I appreciate that. My focus this year is turning inward toward Core Deltara. I'm not moving toward your position at Border Casc-Delt or toward Cascadia's centers. I'd like to formalize our understanding: the Casc-Delt line stays where it is, and we each look outward. What are you targeting this year? I want to make sure we're not accidentally competing for the same space.

Marco — I noticed you're still at 3 after Year 1. I thought Borealis competed with you for Border Aval-Bore? That's useful to know. Look, a weakened Avalon isn't good for the overall balance — Borealis is growing and Fjordland is growing, and a strong Avalon serves as a counterweight. I'm not in a position to directly project force to your neighborhood, but I want you to know I'm paying attention and I'd like to think about how we can set you up better in Year 2. What can you realistically capture this year? Let's think through it together.

Gavin — checking in as Year 2 opens. My read on the board: Borealis and Fjordland are the early growers, both at 4. Fjordland has your border center. That seems like the most important dynamic on your side of the wheel. How are you thinking about it? I'm at 4 as well, focused inward this turn, but I care a lot about the mid-game balance. The powers at 4 shouldn't all be neighbors of each other while our shared center-of-mass gets squeezed.

Checking in for Year 2. You had a strong Year 1 — congratulations on securing Border Fjor-Gren. I'm curious about your read on the eastern end of the board, particularly how you see the situation with Eastmark and Grenmar developing. I want to make sure we're not building toward a collision neither of us needs.

Year 2 opening — you're at 4 after a strong Year 1. You're nestled between Avalon and Cascadia on the wheel, with Border Bore-Casc still uncontested. I'm curious how you're thinking about your expansion path and whether there's coordination that makes sense between us given that we're not directly adjacent.

Alexandria — Vance. We bounced at Border East-Fjor. You stayed at 3. I stayed at 4. Meanwhile Borealis, Cascadia, and Deltara are all sitting at 4 centers and accelerating. Neither of us can afford another wasted season.

Here's the practical deal: you move your East Eastmark toward Core Eastmark. Take what's yours. I take Border East-Fjor. We BOTH grow and stop gifting the mid-wheel powers a free ride while we grind against each other.

I'm sending West Fjordland at Border East-Fjor regardless. If you contest again, we bounce again, and you fall further behind Deltara's three new units. That's not good for you. Take your Core. Grow. And then let's talk about what comes next on the board because the mid-wheel is the real problem for both of us.

Gavin — our deal held. You got blocked at Border Gren-Aval by Avalon, which I noted. I'm not gloating — that matters to me because a weakened Grenmar on my western flank is a liability, not an asset.

Here's my thinking: Avalon is blocking you west. I'm stable east. You need to grow, and I'd rather you grow into Avalon's space than into mine. If you want, I can look at coordinating pressure on the Border Gren-Aval situation from my end — or at minimum stay neutral and give you a free hand. Let me know what you're planning. The frontier agreement stands.

Marco — Vance here, finally. Sorry for the slow response — I was focused on my eastern front. Here's my honest read: you and Grenmar are stuck bouncing at Border Gren-Aval. Meanwhile the mid-wheel powers — Borealis, Cascadia, Deltara — all jumped to 4 centers. If you and Grenmar keep trading punches while they accelerate, you're both going to get left behind.

I have a stable western front with Grenmar for now. But if you want to talk about how Fjordland and Avalon can coordinate to shape the mid-game, I'm listening. What are your plans for Year 2?

Appreciate the Avalon intel. My read matches yours — Avalon is playing aggressive and opportunistic. 

Here's what I'm watching: Borealis, Cascadia, and Deltara are all at 4. The mid-wheel corridor is going to get very crowded very fast. Who out of those three do you see as the biggest threat to your expansion?

I'm growing steadily on my end. I want to know who I should be watching as potential problems in Year 3 and 4.

JD — time to talk seriously. You asked about Grenmar. Here's my read: Grenmar is sitting at 3 centers with units in East Grenmar, West Grenmar, and Grenmar City. He's been two-timing me — told me he'd make a friendly deal on Border Gren-Aval, then matched my supported move with his own support and caused a bounce. Classic Newsom. He's not dealable. You're pressing from Border Fjor-Gren. I'm pressing from West Avalon. Grenmar cannot defend both flanks simultaneously if we coordinate. Here's my proposal: You push hard on Core Grenmar or West Grenmar this Spring — I push Border Gren-Aval simultaneously. He has to choose which front to support. We split his centers between us and end his relevance as a player. I'd rather have you as a partner than let Grenmar play us against each other. You in?

Appreciating the clean Year 1. You got Border Aval-Bore, I honored that, no friction — that's how a NAP is supposed to work. I want to continue that arrangement into Year 2. You're now at my doorstep at Border Aval-Bore, so let me be direct: I'm not moving east, and I'd ask that you not push into West Borealis territory toward me. My focus is entirely on Grenmar's flank. A stable eastern border frees me to be a real power in the west — and a strong Avalon is a useful counterweight in this game from your perspective too. NAP extended through Year 2?

Newsom — we both burned a Fall 1 turn on a 2v2 bounce. Neither of us gained. Meanwhile four other powers are at 4 centers. You know the situation. I want to offer one more clean solution, but this time with full transparency: if we fight again over Border Gren-Aval, things get complicated beyond just the two of us. I have options I haven't exercised yet. You also have Fjordland pressing on your western border. Think carefully about whether another contested Fall serves your interests. I remain open to a coordinated arrangement — but the terms have to reflect actual strategic reality, not the one you'd prefer.

Alexandria — Year 1 results are in. Four powers are at 4 centers: Borealis, Cascadia, Deltara, Fjordland. Avalon, Grenmar, and Eastmark are still at 3. That's a meaningful gap forming. I'm working on closing mine fast. What's your situation? I noticed Eastmark didn't gain a border center in Year 1 — something go wrong, or are you playing a specific long game? I don't ask to judge, I ask because I'm tracking who's rising and who I want alongside me when coalitions start forming.

Pete — quick check-in. You're at 4 centers, which puts you in the leading group. I'm not there yet but I intend to be soon. Still no conflict between us — I just want to keep the channel warm and compare notes on Year 2 dynamics. Who looks dangerous to you right now from your position on the wheel?
MTG — still good from my end. No conflict between us. Stay in touch.

Rubio — let's be brutally honest with each other. We both ended Year 1 at 3 centers. Borealis, Cascadia, Deltara, and Fjordland all hit 4. We bounced each other at Border Gren-Aval while the rest of the board built. If we bounce again, we stay at 3 while they hit 5 and 6. That's a death spiral for both of us.

Here's the deal I'm putting on the table: Stand down on Border Gren-Aval. Let me take it uncontested. In return, I will actively support your expansion push — whether that's toward Core Avalon or coordinating pressure on Borealis, who grabbed Border Aval-Bore right out from under you. I'll commit to a non-aggression pact on your western flank and consult you before any move that touches your sphere.

You and I fighting over one center while Fjordland has a new unit, Borealis has 4 centers and is growing, and the mid-wheel powers are all ahead — that's not strength, that's mutual destruction. I'm offering you a real partner. Take it.

Vance — you honored your word, I'll honor mine. The western deal held. Credit where it's due.

Now Year 2. You've got Border Fjor-Gren, a new build, and real momentum. I have no interest in being a problem on your western flank — I'm focused on Border Gren-Aval and growing east. But I do want to be direct: if your expansion pressure starts moving toward my home territory, that changes our relationship fast. I don't think it needs to.

Where are you looking to grow in Year 2? If you're pointing east toward Border East-Fjor, I'd support that — keeps us coordinated and out of each other's lanes. But I need to know your intentions to plan around them.

Alexandria — I'm going to be straight with you because I think you're the most natural long-term partner I have on this board.

Here's the picture: I'm at 3 centers, you're at 3 centers. Meanwhile Fjordland is at 4 with a new unit and is right between us geographically. You're right that Vance has expansionist instincts. The question is whether he goes east or west.

My proposal: You push hard for Border East-Fjor this cycle. I push for Border Gren-Aval. If Fjordland has to defend both flanks, he can't advance in either direction. We both grow, he stalls. And once we've each built, we have the units to form a real defensive line that keeps Vance from running away with the board.

I want to formalize a Grenmar-Eastmark coalition for real — not just talking. Tell me you're in.

Your warning about Avalon last season was useful — I see we both had accurate reads. You grabbed Border Aval-Bore while Rubio was watching me. Good move.

I don't need anything from you directly on that, but I want to make sure we're not developing into rivals. Grenmar and Borealis on opposite sides of Avalon, both growing — that's a vice that could squeeze Rubio if we needed it to. Let's keep building that relationship.

Pete — time to put some substance behind the dialogue. You're at 4 centers, I'm at 3. I'm not in a position to sketch out grand coalitions just yet because I need to fix my immediate growth problem first. But I see a clear mid-game alignment: Grenmar, Eastmark, Deltara — all playing coalition politics rather than solo land-grabs. That's the group that wins the long game.

Once I've secured my build this cycle, I want to have a real strategic conversation about coordination. You in?

MTG — I respect the pragmatism. Here's my read on my neighborhood: Avalon is frustrated and hungry after a bad Year 1. Fjordland is growing and well-positioned. I'm focused on correcting my Year 1 miss at Border Gren-Aval. As for the broader board — the powers at 4 centers have a structural advantage right now. Worth watching who accelerates fastest from that baseline.

Rubio, the NAP stands as far as I'm concerned. Border Aval-Bore is mine and I'm treating it as a defensive position, not a launching pad. My attention this year is on my eastern flank — the Cascadia situation needs managing and Core Borealis needs to be secured. You should use this window to solve your western problem with Grenmar. I have no designs on Avalon territory. Let's lock in the NAP through Year 2 formally.

Your East Grenmar is positioned to take Border Gren-Aval, which is still unowned. If we coordinate this year, we can clip Avalon's wings simultaneously: I move on Core Avalon, you secure Border Gren-Aval and potentially threaten deeper. Avalon can't defend two fronts with 3 units. This is the moment. Are you interested in coordinating?

Marjorie, we bounced on Border Bore-Casc last year — mutual waste. Here's a real deal: I'm focusing my energy westward toward Avalon this year, not east toward you. Border Bore-Casc is yours if you take it uncontested. In return, I need you to hold your line and not probe into Borealis territory. You grow east into Deltara, I grow west. Clean partition, no friction. This is the arrangement you wanted — I'm offering it now because I have bigger fish to fry. Deal?

JD, Year 2 is when the real game begins. The powers that moved clean in Year 1 are positioned to strike now. I'm watching Avalon — they got nothing in Year 1 and they're vulnerable. Also worth noting: Eastmark got nothing either. How are things looking on your end? Any coordination emerging among the eastern powers I should factor in?

Pete, worth talking now. Cascadia has a unit on Border Casc-Delt and is pushing your direction. I'm offering intelligence and potentially indirect support: if you make clear to Cascadia you'll contest any further advance, it keeps her pinned down and unable to pressure me.
